start.text: the throat $r = r_0$, the bifurcation sphere, where the other exterior begins

legend: the exterior $r > r_0$ that $t$ and $r$ cover
the same radii on the other exterior
the throat $r = r_0$, where the slice crosses the horizon

views.settings: $D = 5$, $r_0 = 1$, the unit of every length, and $r_1 = r_0/2$, $r_2 = r_0$, $r_3 = 3r_0/2$, on the plane of $r$ and $\phi$ ($\psi = \theta = \pi/2$).
caption: The plane of $r$ and $\phi$ ($\psi = \theta = \pi/2$) of the hole of three charges ($r_1 = r_0/2$, $r_2 = r_0$, $r_3 = 3r_0/2$) at one moment of $t$, drawn as a surface in flat space with every distance along it the metric distance. On it the metric is $(H_1H_2H_3)^{1/3}(dr^2/f + r^2d\phi^2)$, so the circle of coordinate radius $r$ has the circumference radius $r(H_1H_2H_3)^{1/6}$, which is $1.42\,r_0$ at the throat $r = r_0$ where Tangherlini's is $r_0$.
Every slice of constant $t$ passes through the bifurcation sphere $r = r_0$, where the circles are smallest, and runs on through it into a second exterior, the same surface turned over.

views.label: Extreme, three charges

start.text: the throat runs on without end toward the horizon $r = 0$, its circles closing on the circumference radius $1\,r_2$

legend: one moment of $t$, which $t$ and $r > 0$ cover

views.settings: $D = 5$, $r_2 = 1$, the unit of every length, and $r_1 = r_2/2$, $r_3 = 2r_2$, on the plane of $r$ and $\phi$ ($\psi = \theta = \pi/2$).
caption: The plane of $r$ and $\phi$ ($\psi = \theta = \pi/2$) of the extreme hole of three charges ($r_1 = r_2/2$, $r_3 = 2r_2$) at one moment of $t$, drawn as a surface in flat space with every distance along it the metric distance. On it the metric is $(H_1H_2H_3)^{1/3}(dr^2 + r^2d\phi^2)$, and toward the horizon $r = 0$ it tends to $(r_1r_2r_3)^{2/3}(dr^2/r^2 + d\phi^2)$.

The surface falls without end while its circles close on the radius $(r_1r_2r_3)^{1/3} = r_2$: the throat is infinitely long, and it is drawn down to $r = r_2/50$. The 3-sphere at its end has the area $2\pi^2r_1r_2r_3$, which vanishes when a charge is missing.

views.label: Equal charges

start.text: the throat $\rho = 5r_q/4$, the bifurcation sphere, where the other exterior begins

legend: the same radii on the other exterior
the throat $\rho = 5r_q/4$, where the slice crosses the horizon

views.settings: $D = 5$, $r_q = 1$, the unit of every length, and $r_0 = 3r_q/4$, so that the horizons are at $\rho = 5r_q/4$ and $\rho = r_q$, on the plane of $\rho$ and $\phi$ ($\psi = \theta = \pi/2$).
caption: The plane of $\rho$ and $\phi$ ($\psi = \theta = \pi/2$) of the hole of three equal charges ($r_0 = 3r_q/4$) at one moment of $t$, drawn as a surface in flat space with every distance along it the metric distance. On it the metric is $d\rho^2/((1 - 25r_q^2/16\rho^2)(1 - r_q^2/\rho^2)) + \rho^2d\phi^2$, the equator of the Reissner-Nordström black hole of five dimensions.
Every slice of constant $t$ passes through the bifurcation sphere $\rho = 5r_q/4$, where the circles are smallest, and runs on through it into a second exterior, the same surface turned over.

On it the metric is $\sqrt{H_1H_2H_3H_4}\,(dr^2/f + r^2d\phi^2)$, so the circle of coordinate radius $r$ has the circumference radius $r(H_1H_2H_3H_4)^{1/4}$, which is $2.18\,r_0$ at the throat $r = r_0$ where Schwarzschild's is $r_0$.
Every slice of constant $t$ passes through the bifurcation sphere $r = r_0$, where the circles are smallest, and runs on through it into a second exterior, the same surface turned over.

views.label: Extreme, four charges

start.text: the throat runs on without end toward the horizon $r = 0$, its circles closing on the circumference radius $1.107\,r_2$

legend: one moment of $t$, which $t$ and $r > 0$ cover

views.settings: $D = 4$, $r_2 = 1$, the unit of every length, and $r_1 = r_2/2$, $r_3 = 3r_2/2$, $r_4 = 2r_2$, on the equator ($\theta = \pi/2$).
caption: The equatorial plane ($\theta = \pi/2$) of the extreme hole of four charges ($r_1 = r_2/2$, $r_3 = 3r_2/2$, $r_4 = 2r_2$) at one moment of $t$, drawn as a surface in flat space with every distance along it the metric distance. On it the metric is $\sqrt{H_1H_2H_3H_4}\,(dr^2 + r^2d\phi^2)$, and toward the horizon $r = 0$ it tends to $\sqrt{r_1r_2r_3r_4}\,(dr^2/r^2 + d\phi^2)$, Bertotti-Robinson's cylinder.

The surface falls without end while its circles close on the radius $(r_1r_2r_3r_4)^{1/4} = 1.11\,r_2$: the throat is infinitely long, and it is drawn down to $r = r_2/50$. The sphere at its end has the area $4\pi\sqrt{r_1r_2r_3r_4}$, which vanishes when a charge is missing.
